Another name for it is Järv, and in English it is called the wolverine.
It has broad paws with which it can walk well over snow.
The wolverine does not occur in the wild in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The wolverine grows to about 65 to 105 centimetres long, plus a bushy tail. Males usually weigh 11 to 18 kilograms, and females less. That makes it clearly bigger and heavier than most other **mustelids** such as the stone marten or weasels. Its thick, dark brown coat often has a light band on the sides. It has strong legs, big **claws** and powerful jaws.

The wolverine lives in the cold regions around the North Pole, in **coniferous forests** and in the tundra. It is found in Norway, Sweden, Finland, Russia, Siberia, Canada and Alaska. It needs very large territories, sometimes several hundred square kilometres. Its thick coat and broad paws, which work like **snowshoes**, protect it in winter.

The wolverine is an **omnivore** with a liking for meat. It hunts hares, rodents and birds and can even catch reindeer in deep snow. Very often it eats **carrion**, for example the leftovers of wolf kills. With its strong teeth it also cracks frozen meat and bones. It hides stores in the snow for later.

Wolverines are mostly loners and cover long distances in search of food. They are brave and can even drive wolves or bears away from a carcass. In late winter the female usually gives birth to two or three young in a **snow den**. The deep snow protects the young from cold and enemies.

In Scandinavia the wolverine is unpopular with reindeer herders, because it sometimes kills reindeer. In the past it was heavily hunted, and today it is protected in many countries. In Switzerland it does not live in the wild, but you can see it in some **wildlife parks**. The German name Vielfrass probably comes from the Old Norse fjallfress, which means mountain cat, and was later misunderstood.

begriffe.erklaerung: A family of predators with a long body, such as the badger, otter and weasel.
The flesh of animals that are already dead.
An animal that lives alone most of the time.
The area in which an animal lives and which it defends.

gewusst: The comic character Wolverine from the X-Men is named after the wolverine.
A wolverine can walk dozens of kilometres through snow in a day.
The wolverine's fur hardly ices up, which is why the Inuit used it in the past for the edges of hoods.

teile.einleitung: The wood mouse is a small, nimble mouse with big eyes, big ears and a long tail. It lives almost everywhere in Switzerland, in woods, fields and gardens. Because it is out and about mainly at night, you still only rarely get to see it.
wichtigste: The wood mouse likes living best in woods, fields and gardens.
In Switzerland it is found almost everywhere.
It is active mainly at night and avoids bright light.
Its big eyes show that it can see well in the dark.
The tail is almost as long as the body.
On the belly it has light, almost white fur.
In the wild, a wood mouse usually lives only about a year.

abschnitte.text: Without the tail, the wood mouse is about 8 to 11 centimetres long and usually weighs between 15 and 30 grams. Its back is brown, and on the belly it has light, almost white fur. The tail is almost as long as the body. Big **button eyes** and big ears show that it can see and hear well in the dark.

The wood mouse lives in woods, hedges, fields and gardens and is found in almost all of Europe. In Switzerland you find it almost everywhere, from the lowlands up into the mountains. It digs **burrows** with tunnels and nest chambers or uses hollows under roots. In winter it sometimes also comes into garden sheds and cellars.

The wood mouse eats mainly seeds and fruits such as acorns, beechnuts, hazelnuts and berries. It also likes to eat buds and young shoots, and also insects, caterpillars and snails. When eating, it holds the food cleverly with its front paws. If it finds more than it needs, it makes **stores** and hides them for later.

The wood mouse is active at night and avoids bright light, and in danger it hides in a flash. It has a very good sense of smell and hearing, which helps it to find food. With its strong hind legs it can make long **leaps** and also climbs well. If an enemy grabs it by the tail, the skin of the tail can come off, and the mouse escapes.

From spring to autumn a female has several litters, usually of four to seven young. The gestation lasts only about three to four weeks. The young are born naked and blind and are independent after a few weeks. Because many wood mice die young, the many young make sure that the species survives.

The wood mouse is an important prey animal for the **tawny owl**, fox, weasel, marten and cats. In the wild it therefore usually lives only about a year. Because it leaves forgotten stores in the ground, it helps to spread trees such as oak and beech. It is easy to confuse with the very similar **yellow-necked mouse**, which has a yellowish patch at the throat.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mammal with gnawing teeth that keep growing all its life.
Food that an animal hides in order to eat it later.
An animal that is awake at night and sleeps by day.
All the young that a mother animal gives birth to at once.

gewusst: Wood mice are skilful climbers and even climb into bushes and trees to get at fruit.
Wood mice sometimes mark their way with small leaves or twigs in order to find their way around.

teile.einleitung: Varroa destructor is a tiny mite that attacks honey bees and does them great harm. It sucks on bees and their brood and passes on dangerous viruses. Together with the lack of flowering meadows, it is today one of the greatest threats to honey bees.
wichtigste: Varroa destructor is a mite that lives as a parasite on honey bees.
It is about 1.6 millimetres wide and reddish brown.
The varroa mite and a lack of flowering meadows especially threaten honey bees today.
The mite multiplies in the capped brood cells of the bees.
It originally comes from the Eastern honey bee in Asia.
In Switzerland it was first discovered in 1984.
Without treatment by beekeepers, most infested colonies die within a few years.

abschnitte.text: Varroa destructor is a **mite**, that is, an arachnid with eight legs. The female is about 1.1 millimetres long and 1.6 millimetres wide, reddish brown and flat like a scale. It lives as a **parasite** on honey bees and feeds on the fat body of the bees. The name destructor means destroyer.

abschnitte.titel: How does it harm the bees?
abschnitte.text: The female mites slip into the **brood cells** with the bee larvae shortly before they are capped. There they lay eggs, and the young mites feed on the growing bee. The bees that hatch are weakened and live shorter lives. What is especially bad is that the mite passes on **viruses**, such as the deformed wing virus, which gives bees crippled wings.

Originally the mite lived on the **Eastern honey bee** in Asia, which can defend itself well against it. In the 20th century it jumped to our Western honey bee. Through the trade in bee colonies it spread almost worldwide. It reached Switzerland in 1984, and today there are hardly any colonies without varroa.

Beekeepers have to **treat** their colonies against the mite every year. Natural acids such as formic acid and oxalic acid are often used. They also remove the drone brood, in which especially many mites multiply. With a tray in the beehive, beekeepers count the mites that have fallen down and so check how bad the infestation is.

Besides the varroa mite, bees suffer from the lack of **flowering meadows** and hedges. Pesticides and long spells of bad weather also weaken the colonies. Everyone can help by planting native flowers in the garden or on the balcony. Researchers in Switzerland, for example at the Agroscope bee research centre in Bern, are looking for new solutions against the mite.

begriffe.erklaerung: A very small arachnid with eight legs.
A living thing that lives on or in another and harms it.
A honeycomb cell in which a bee larva grows up.
A person who keeps bees and collects honey.

gewusst: Without treatment by beekeepers, there are hardly any wild honey bee colonies left in Europe.
Transferred to a bee, a varroa mite would be as big as a plate on a person.
The mite prefers drone brood, because it stays capped for longer.

teile.einleitung: The eagle owl is a mighty owl with bright orange eyes and striking ear tufts. It is often regarded as the largest species of owl in the world and is a night hunter with very fine hearing. In Switzerland it nests mainly on rock faces in the Alps, in the Jura and in Ticino.
wichtigste: The eagle owl is often called the largest species of owl in the world.
Its eyes are typically orange.
Its hearing is much more sensitive than ours and helps it to locate prey in the dark.
With its very strong claws it grips and kills its prey.
The female usually lays 2 to 3 eggs and sits on them mainly alone.
Young eagle owls leave the nest before they can fly and clamber about as branchers.
Eagle owls react very sensitively to disturbance at the nesting site.

abschnitte.text: The eagle owl grows to about 60 to 75 centimetres tall and has a wingspan of up to 1.7 metres. The females are clearly bigger and heavier than the males and weigh up to about 3 kilograms. Its plumage is brown and yellowish with dark streaks, which makes it well **camouflaged**. Striking are the long **ear tufts** and the big orange eyes. It is often called the largest owl in the world, and only the Blakiston's fish owl in East Asia is similar in size.

Eagle owls live in Europe, Asia and North Africa. They need quiet nesting places, mostly on **rock faces**, in quarries or on steep slopes, and open country to hunt in. In Switzerland an estimated few hundred pairs nest, mainly in the Alps, in the Jura and in Ticino. Eagle owls stay in their territory all year round.

The eagle owl hunts at dusk and at night. With its very sensitive **hearing** and good eyes it finds prey even in the dark, and thanks to soft feathers it flies almost silently. It eats mice, rats, hedgehogs, hares and birds such as crows and pigeons. A strong eagle owl can occasionally even overpower young foxes or other birds of prey. Indigestible remains such as hair and bones it coughs up again as **pellets**.

How many eggs a female lays depends on the **food supply**, and it is mostly 2 to 3. The female sits on the eggs mainly alone for about five weeks. The male supplies her with food during this time. The young leave the nest before they can really fly and clamber about in the surroundings as **branchers**. If the parents are disturbed at the nesting site, they may even abandon the brood.

In the past the eagle owl was heavily persecuted and had almost disappeared in many areas. Today it is protected in Switzerland, but is still on the **Red List** of threatened breeding birds. Many eagle owls die on power lines, in road traffic or on fences. Climbers and photographers should avoid nesting cliffs during the breeding season. Wild eagle owls can live to be about 20 years old.

The German name Uhu comes from its deep call “buho”, which can be heard far away in late winter. With the call the male marks his **territory** and attracts a female. Often male and female call in a duet. In many legends and fairy tales the owl is a symbol of wisdom.

begriffe.erklaerung: Tufts of feathers on the head that look like ears but have nothing to do with hearing.
A ball of indigestible hair and bones that owls cough up.
A young owl that has left the nest but cannot really fly yet.
An area that an animal claims for itself and defends.

gewusst: An eagle owl can turn its head by up to 270 degrees.
The ear openings of the eagle owl lie hidden under the plumage at the edge of the face and not in the ear tufts.
In the eagle owl the female is bigger than the male, as in many birds of prey.
